spec_match.rationale: Covers the explainer's standalone-dropdown scenario (button command/commandfor → menulist) plus the machinery statement — menulist behaves as popover=auto — by pairing it with the plain [popover] baseline that demonstrates exactly which behaviors are inherited vs menu-specific.

interactive.rationale: The native invoker button and menuitems are live where supported; the command-keyword matrix executes real invocations per keyword; the popover baseline is fully interactive on every modern engine.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Index blurb promises the live command-keyword matrix and the popover baseline; delivered.

edge_cases.rationale: The matrix treats the accepted command set as build-dependent truth rather than documentation — a first-draft claim that only the generic popover commands work was corrected after the flag run proved toggle-menu/show-menu are honoured on the dev-trial build. Rejected keywords are caught so they can't break the matrix.

references.rationale: Feature index cites https://chromestatus.com/feature/5206029088063488; the code block shows both explainer and generic wirings.

conformance.rationale: The suite's menulist-implicit-popover assertion is this page's foundation check.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 CDP: bare run — baseline popover opened via popovertarget, item activation closed it, native panel honestly inert with the matrix marked not-runnable; flag run — the real button opened the menulist (:popover-open true), Duplicate activated, and the matrix measured show-popover/toggle-popover/toggle-menu/show-menu all opening on this build. Zero console errors; 0px overflow both classes; screenshots read.

telemetry_health.rationale: menuelem-button-menulist-loaded asserts with the native flag.

design_system.rationale: Panels and menus use border-black on ivory, stone status blocks, emerald/rose matrix verdicts; baseline menu buttons override background AND color; CSS variables only.

accessibility.rationale: Baseline invoker carries explicit aria-haspopup=menu and the menu role/aria-label with role=menuitem children (the manual work the native element does implicitly); matrix output aria-live; status role=status; native panel documents that its implicit ARIA lives in the accessibility tree, not content attributes.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Single-column panels; menus within panel width; 0px overflow at 360×740 DPR3 and 1280×2000.

openQuestions.title: Matrix on the current surface, plus implicit ARIA verification
openQuestions.detail: Capture the accepted-keyword set on a current-surface build (does the explainer's dedicated toggle-menu remain? do the generic popover commands stay valid?), and inspect the accessibility tree to confirm the invoking button's implicit aria-haspopup=menu/aria-expanded — content attributes correctly stay absent, so only an AX-tree inspection can show it.

openQuestions.title: Focus-move-on-open behavior
openQuestions.detail: The explainer says focus should move to the menulist's first focusable item on invocation, unlike generic popovers; not verifiable on the early build — test on a current one.

guidanceConsulted.query: popover invoker commandfor light dismiss baseline
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Prefer native popover/invoker wiring over custom open-close scripting.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Baseline uses pure popovertarget wiring — the only script is item activation; the native panel uses command/commandfor.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Anchor dropdown overlays to their invoker and rely on light dismiss.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Native menulist uses its implicit anchor; baseline validated for light dismiss/Esc via the popover API.

summary: Verified headlessly (no chrome-devtools-mcp in this cloud session): the popover baseline was driven for real on the bare engine, and the flag run proved the native invoker path end-to-end — including a live command-keyword matrix whose evidence corrected this page's own first-draft claim about which keywords engines accept.
